newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 24.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - An unnamed member of the board of the central bank said a decision will be made today about decreasing the bank's basic rates.
- The Czech National Bank had losses last year of 8.65 billion crowns. According to the governer of the bank, the losses were caused by losses from the value of the crown last year.
- The Industry and Trade Ministry and Ceskomoravska Zarucni a Rozvojova Banka are preparing help for small importers, measures which should be ready in about one week.

- Austrian Voest Alpine is planning to establish a joint company with Nova Hut and sign a contract to supply technology, which will cost about 400 million dollars and will be the largest investment in the Czech metal industry in the last 10 years.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The opposition Social Democrats, whose bank accounts have been blocked for a few days for not paying taxes, are attempting to make their case look like a political attempt to get rid of their party, the paper says.
- President Vaclav Havel returned from his vacation yesterday, and he will fly to Bonn today to meet with members of the German parliament.
- The Prague company Kvestar won the tender for Chemopharma, the largest domestic manufacturer of plasters, because Kvestar has experience in reviving large businesses.
- The investment company Expandia won the tender for a new administrator of the holding fund Agrobanka.
- American Motorola International Development Corporation obtained a 57 percent stake in Tesla Sezam.
LIDOVE NOVINY - The Czech Army should obtain a loan of about 2.4 billion crowns from the United States, according to a proposal from the Defence Ministry approved by the cabinet yesterday.
- The cabinet will issue credits amounting to about 2.5 billion crowns to indebted hospitals and insurance companies.
- The cabinet proposes to cover last year's budget deficit with government bonds, according to Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik.
- Rudolf Mladek, the former director of Czech Railways will become an advisor to Transport Minister Martin Riman next month.
PRAVO - On Wednesday, the cabinet named Augustin Hrboticky as the head of the commission for fighting economic criminality. He will enter the position immediately.
- Motoinvest lost its legal dispute with Nova Television, in which the financial group had asked for a public opology for a remark made on the news last September.
- Daewoo Avia increased its sales during the first quarter of this year by 5.8 percent, year-on-year, and sold 939 vehicles. Avia's exports increased by 10 percent to 260 vehicles.
